question: Why does next/image require configuring `images.remotePatterns` in next.config.ts for external image URLs?
options: To prevent your Next.js image optimizer from acting as an open proxy that fetches and processes arbitrary malicious third-party URLs
Because browsers refuse to render HTTPS images without a server-side allowlist
To convert all PNG files into SVG vectors during development
Because next/image disables caching unless remotePatterns has at least three hostnames
explanation: Allowlisting explicit hostnames and paths in remotePatterns protects your server from being abused as an open image-optimization proxy for untrusted external URLs.

question: Which combination of next/image props is best for an above-the-fold hero banner inside a fixed-aspect responsive container?
options: loading='lazy' without width, height, or sizes
priority paired with explicit width/height (or fill + sizes) so the browser preloads the LCP asset and reserves space to prevent CLS
unoptimized={true} on every image across the entire site
omitting alt text so the image decodes faster
explanation: Setting priority preloads the above-the-fold LCP image instead of lazy-loading it, while width/height or fill + sizes prevents Cumulative Layout Shift and serves appropriately sized srcset candidates.

question: How does next/font eliminate external font network waterfalls and layout shift in production?
options: It renders all typography inside HTML <canvas> elements
It skips custom fonts on mobile devices and forces Times New Roman
It downloads and self-hosts font files at build time and applies automatic size-adjust fallback CSS metrics
It injects a blocking synchronous XHR request inside beforeInteractive scripts
explanation: next/font bundles font assets at build time so no runtime request goes to external font CDNs, and computes fallback font metrics to prevent layout shifts.

question: Which next/script strategy should you choose for a non-critical customer support chat widget so it does not delay hydration?
options: beforeInteractive
afterInteractive
syncBlocking
lazyOnload
explanation: lazyOnload defers loading non-essential scripts like chat widgets until browser idle time after page resources have loaded, keeping hydration fast.

question: What happens if you name a database password `NEXT_PUBLIC_DB_PASSWORD` and reference it inside a Client Component?
options: Next.js throws a compile error and deletes the variable
Next.js inlines the secret string directly into the public client JavaScript bundle at build time, exposing it to every visitor
Next.js encrypts the variable using the user's session cookie
The variable evaluates to undefined in the browser because passwords are filtered automatically
explanation: Any environment variable prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ is statically embedded into the browser JavaScript bundle at build time. Secrets must remain unprefixed and stay strictly on the server.
